newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Golf-Olazabal to break new ground in Irish Open.
newsitem.headline: Golf-Olazabal to break new ground in Irish Open.

text.p: Jose Maria Olazabal will break new ground on his comeback from foot problems when he tees off in the Irish Open on Thursday.
Olazabal has restricted himself to playing two successive tournaments since his return from an 18-month layoff.

But the Irish Open will be the first of three he plans to play in the next three weeks. The other two are the Loch Lomond World Invitational and the British Open. Olazabal, who has risen to 11th in Europe's Ryder Cup table in just four months, said on Wednesday: "After the U.S. Open I spent two weeks at home and for three or four days did nothing.
"Since then I've practised and done exercises for my feet. To test the feet, I then played virtually every day last week.
"While I know I'm not 100 per cent...I'm at the stage where now I'm going to play three weeks in a row for the first time and see how I go."
Olazabal won the 1990 Irish Open but lost a playoff for the title to Nick Faldo two years later.
Faldo, now a regular on the US Tour, also begins a three-week stint in Europe when he plays in the Irish Open, an event he won three successive times from 1991.
Faldo, 26th in the Ryder Cup table, is keen to excel in all three tournaments in Europe to gain an automatic Ryder Cup spot.
"I've got just four events to make it," he said. "These three and the US PGA Championship, so obviously I want to try to win one and do well in the others and then I'll be in."
But Faldo is not worried if that does not happen.
"If I'm there, I'm there. But if not then we are always likely to pick someone with experience.
"I have that and I have won in America this year, so I don't think that's far off what I'm supposed to be doing to get into the team."
Other leading players competing in the Irish Open at Druids Glen just outside Dublin include defending champion Colin Montgomerie, Bernhard Langer and Ian Woosnam.
